The August Customer.io forecast estimated 1,620,000 baseline messages, 240,000 routine-campaign messages, and 110,000 transactional messages against a 2,000,000-message monthly allowance. Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The quarterly access review retained only existing scopes: Ines for lifecycle preflight and bounded routine-send release, Daniela’s engineering group for integration release and rollback, and Riley for customer correction and incident-stop decisions. The review added no authority.

The Helio Start paid-test decision was finalized in August. The fixed cohort contained 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17. Eighteen became paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860, and certified support effort was 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; five of 25 exceeded 90 support minutes, and four of those required coordination with a separate owner-level permission or network-allowlist holder. Priya and Riley did not authorize a second Q3 batch. Paid traffic remained off through September 30, with no additional budget, pipeline or forecast credit, and no implication of causal acquisition, revenue, support improvement, scale readiness, or forecast impact. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. Any later proposal requires Customer Success to define staffed ownership and service hours for the coordination, plus a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight by Daniela and Ines showing preserved paid-source final-route attribution, governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, and suppression behavior. Account-level support minutes must continue from first contact without resetting the clock.

Customer Success’s coordination-design brief initially lacked a capacity assumption. The completed design names the Customer Success setup desk as primary owner, with the on-duty Customer Success manager as backup, during 8:00am–6:00pm Central Monday through Friday. It can support a future capped run of no more than 25 admitted workspaces without displacing ordinary assisted coverage. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Owen’s formal H2 mature-outcome-packet goal was later marked met because he used the correct denominator and dates, waited for all predeclared windows, led with owner certifications and measurement limits, and found no semantic dispute. This did not transfer board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority; any future semantic dispute requires him to leave the review incomplete and escalate it. Ines’s connector-specific instructional-wording goal was also marked met after she independently carried a revision through review, supplied paired cases, preserved governed meanings, and left connector detection and release verification with Daniela. Her release ceiling and other authority limits remained unchanged.

The shared-state Customer Success auto-nudge system initially had four production consumers. Riley rejected Growth’s proposal to add a renewal-risk notification as a fifth because semantic mapping, field mapping, source-owner review, freshness limits, operator views, and rollback rehearsal were incomplete. The production feed remained at four consumers. The denominator rule remained one primary ledger row per scheduled nudge decision, with checks, holds, evaluation timestamps, and final disposition preserved in audit history; rechecks and holds did not create duplicate denominator rows.

A May 20 refresh caused 12 pending decisions to cross the freshness limit. The system held all 12 rather than reusing stale “no work” values. After the source was restored, fresh checks found eight with current active adoption or renewal work, becoming valid suppressions, and four with current no-work state, proceeding. No stale-state nudge was sent, no customer correction was needed, and rollback was unnecessary. Checkpoints recorded 327 unique scheduled decisions through May 22, 641 through May 29, and 846 through June 5, including 19, 31, and 39 fail-closed stale/conflicting decisions respectively. There were no differences across external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, or Customer Success views. Riley treated this as interim evidence, not mature reliability or justification for retiring the legacy path.

In August, Growth’s first historical replay incorrectly omitted active-Customer-Success-work suppression because it argued that an in-product reminder was not a “send.” Riley ruled this a disputed interpretation, kept the replay incomplete, prohibited shadow and production work, and required Growth to implement suppression and rerun it. The corrected 240-record replay found 12 active/current CS-work records suppressed, nine missing or stale required states held fail-closed, and 219 current eligible records; there were no semantic disagreements, cross-surface mismatches, or customer-facing actions. Riley permitted only bounded nonproduction shadow work. The first shadow interval evaluated 96 live decisions: eight suppressed for active CS work, four held for stale state, and 84 reminder-eligible, with zero customer-facing reminders and no semantic or cross-surface disagreement. Riley declined production, requiring a complete shadow review, Riley’s customer-action approval, and Daniela’s release and rollback approval. The production count stayed at four.

The August Customer.io forecast estimated 1,620,000 baseline messages, 240,000 routine-campaign messages, and 110,000 transactional messages against a 2,000,000-message monthly allowance. Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The quarterly access review retained only existing scopes: Ines for lifecycle preflight and bounded routine-send release, Daniela’s engineering group for integration release and rollback, and Riley for customer correction and incident-stop decisions. The review added no authority.

The Helio Start paid-test decision was finalized in August. The fixed cohort contained 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17. Eighteen became paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860, and certified support effort was 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; five of 25 exceeded 90 support minutes, and four of those required coordination with a separate owner-level permission or network-allowlist holder. Paid traffic remained off through September 30, with no additional budget, pipeline or forecast credit, and no implication of causal acquisition, revenue, support improvement, scale readiness, or forecast impact. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. Any later proposal requires Customer Success to define staffed ownership and service hours for the coordination, plus a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight by Daniela and Ines showing preserved paid-source final-route attribution, governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, and suppression behavior. Account-level support minutes must continue from first contact without resetting the clock.

The completed design names the Customer Success setup desk as primary owner, with the on-duty Customer Success manager as backup, during 8:00am–6:00pm Central Monday through Friday. It can support a future capped run of no more than 25 admitted workspaces without displacing ordinary assisted coverage. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. The rejected `Start setup` CTA was replaced by `Get setup help`, while the current CTA had been `Talk to an expert`; all pointed to the Customer Success assisted path. Riley assessed `Get setup help` as honest only if the destination and telemetry remained unchanged. Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Riley’s personal health decisions retained the same conservative method. Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Marcus reported that 18 seniors completed intake-week questionnaires but the week was crowded and some were already spiraling about deadlines. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy matched the preservation-master byte count and full SHA-256, while the local copy differed and remained nonauthoritative. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

**Status:** Historical snapshot — directional evidence only, recorded ahead of the formal H2 ruling (Feb 21, 2023). Not itself a ruling.

**Same-window comparison**
Same-week comp pulled for H2 (seasonal / competitor-cycle hypothesis):
- Feb 2022 mid-seg monthly churn: 2.2%
- Feb 2021 mid-seg monthly churn: 2.0%
- No historical version of the current spike appears in either comparison year.

**Continuity with earlier analysis method**
Comparison used the same cohort logic as the January scan and the Owen check performed the same morning (Feb 20). No change to cut methodology between H1 and H2 analysis.

**Direction the evidence pointed**
Directionally unfavorable to the "comforting explanations": H1 (tier-driven) had already been ruled dead after the tier split came back flat, and this same-window comp pushes against the seasonal / competitor-cycle story as well. Read together, the two results move away from external/benign causes.

**Unresolved quality check at this time**
Denominator handling had not yet been sanity-checked a second time. That check was flagged as outstanding before treating the directional read as confirmed — i.e., before saying it "too loudly." (The pricing-page experiment being run in parallel was not treated as a competing explanation for this cut.)

**Formal ruling status as of this checkpoint:** Not yet issued. H2 was formally ruled out the following day (Feb 21, 2023) once this comparison was locked in alongside the historical comps.

Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

input.body:
**Purpose:** This note exists to prevent readers of the archived experiment record from mistaking the first-week interim checkpoint for the final verdict on `EXP-2023-02-pricing-page` / `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`. The two are separated below.

---

## 1. First-week checkpoint (2023-03-17) — INTERIM, NOT A RESULT

- **What it showed:** Treatment was running roughly **-0.6 pts** vs. control on signup-to-paid conversion.
- **How uncertain it was:** The confidence interval still crossed zero / overlapped noise at that point. This was explicitly **not** treated as conclusive — it was a one-week peek, not a powered read.
- **What we decided at that point:** No action. `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` was left running unchanged, still at its 50% split (live since 2023-03-07), pending the full two-week powered read. Nothing was shipped, rolled back, or otherwise decided on the strength of this checkpoint alone.

## 2. Final powered result (2023-03-20) — the actual verdict

- **What it showed:** The full two-week powered read came in at **-1.8 pts** on signup-to-paid conversion, **p = 0.03**. A cohort-cut rerun (Owen) matched the primary analysis, ruling out a query error or tracking artifact.
- **Decision:** `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` was rolled back to 0% immediately. Experiment status flipped from running to underperforming/rolled back.
- **Postmortem (2023-03-28):** Sent to Marcus Vail, Priya Devarajan, Daniela Schultz, and Tomás Vega. Headline finding was that the test never got a clean read because the **2023-03-02 signup-form layout change** was live concurrently, confounding the -1.8pt result. Framed neutrally (design-review-note → concurrent-change → confounded-result), no name-pointing.

## 3. Why the distinction matters

The two numbers point in the *same direction* (both negative), which could easily read as "the interim checkpoint predicted the outcome." Readers should **not** draw that inference:
- The first-week number was statistically inconclusive on its own and was explicitly not acted on.
- The final number is confounded by the concurrent signup-form layout change and cannot be cleanly attributed to the pricing revision alone.
- The standing rule this episode helped establish — first significance does not ship / does not verdict, hold for a stabilization/powered window — applies here on the interim side, and the no-concurrent-page-change rule applies on the confound side.

## 4. Downstream registry status (for completeness, not part of the read itself)

- `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`: rolled back 2023-03-20, later formally decommissioned 2024-09-20 after confirming no remaining production evaluation or rollback dependency. The experiment record itself (`EXP-2023-02-pricing-page`) was left unaltered — it remains rolled back with its original -1.8pt / p=0.03 result and confounder note.
- A separate, unrelated stale flag (`flag_pricing_page_v3`, created Jan 2023, never wired to any experiment) was decommissioned 2024-07-17. Not connected to this test.

Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. The nudge generated only about $4–$5 expansion MRR per account against an $8 target, with too small a sample for strategic claims. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. In a 312-account table, 118 had at least three integrations, 141 had at least two active administrators, 39 had repeated plan-limit modals, and 37 had blocked ceiling actions. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Its ceiling remained no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week, with active Customer Success work suppressing prompts and handoff rules preserved.

Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Riley’s delegation produced relief but initially raised concern about not reclaiming work. Owen’s formal H2 mature-outcome-packet goal was later marked met because he used the correct denominator and dates, waited for all predeclared windows, led with owner certifications and measurement limits, and found no semantic dispute. This did not transfer board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority; any future semantic dispute requires him to leave the review incomplete and escalate it. Ines’s connector-specific instructional-wording goal was also marked met after she independently carried a revision through review, supplied paired cases, preserved governed meanings, and left connector detection and release verification with Daniela. Her release ceiling and other authority limits remained unchanged.

The shared-state Customer Success auto-nudge system initially had four production consumers. Riley rejected Growth’s proposal to add a renewal-risk notification as a fifth because semantic mapping, field mapping, source-owner review, freshness limits, operator views, and rollback rehearsal were incomplete. The production feed remained at four consumers. The denominator rule remained one primary ledger row per scheduled nudge decision, with checks, holds, evaluation timestamps, and final disposition preserved in audit history; rechecks and holds did not create duplicate denominator rows.

A May 20 refresh caused 12 pending decisions to cross the freshness limit. The system held all 12 rather than reusing stale “no work” values. After the source was restored, fresh checks found eight with current active adoption or renewal work, becoming valid suppressions, and four with current no-work state, proceeding. No stale-state nudge was sent, no customer correction was needed, and rollback was unnecessary. Checkpoints recorded 327 unique scheduled decisions through May 22, 641 through May 29, and 846 through June 5, including 19, 31, and 39 fail-closed stale/conflicting decisions respectively. There were no differences across external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, or Customer Success views. Riley treated this as interim evidence, not mature reliability or justification for retiring the legacy path.

In August, Growth’s first historical replay incorrectly omitted active-Customer-Success-work suppression because it argued that an in-product reminder was not a “send.” Riley ruled this a disputed interpretation, kept the replay incomplete, prohibited shadow and production work, and required Growth to implement suppression and rerun it. The corrected 240-record replay found 12 active/current CS-work records suppressed, nine missing or stale required states held fail-closed, and 219 current eligible records; there were no semantic disagreements, cross-surface mismatches, or customer-facing actions. Riley permitted only bounded nonproduction shadow work. The first shadow interval evaluated 96 live decisions: eight suppressed for active CS work, four held for stale state, and 84 reminder-eligible, with zero customer-facing reminders and no semantic or cross-surface disagreement. Riley declined production, requiring a complete shadow review, Riley’s customer-action approval, and Daniela’s release and rollback approval. The production count stayed at four.

The August Customer.io forecast estimated 1,620,000 baseline messages, 240,000 routine-campaign messages, and 110,000 transactional messages against a 2,000,000-message monthly allowance. Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The quarterly access review retained only existing scopes: Ines for lifecycle preflight and bounded routine-send release, Daniela’s engineering group for integration release and rollback, and Riley for customer correction and incident-stop decisions. The review added no authority.

The Helio Start paid-test decision was finalized in August. The fixed cohort contained 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17. Eighteen became paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860, and certified support effort was 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; five of 25 exceeded 90 support minutes, and four of those required coordination with a separate owner-level permission or network-allowlist holder. Priya and Riley did not authorize a second Q3 batch. Paid traffic remained off through September 30, with no additional budget, pipeline or forecast credit, and no implication of causal acquisition, revenue, support improvement, scale readiness, or forecast impact. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. Any later proposal requires Customer Success to define staffed ownership and service hours for the coordination, plus a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight by Daniela and Ines showing preserved paid-source final-route attribution, governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, and suppression behavior. Account-level support minutes must continue from first contact without resetting the clock.

Customer Success’s coordination-design brief initially lacked a capacity assumption. The completed design names the Customer Success setup desk as primary owner, with the on-duty Customer Success manager as backup, during 8:00am–6:00pm Central Monday through Friday. It can support a future capped run of no more than 25 admitted workspaces without displacing ordinary assisted coverage. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley accepted the staffing section as complete but kept the 24-case preflight and any paid batch pending. The design itself authorizes no batch, budget, traffic, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

Riley also rejected using unused paid-test capacity to increase Expansion Assist to four prompts per week. The proposal neither transferred unused authority nor changed the existing behavior-based eligibility, active-CS suppression, handoff rules, three-exposure ceiling, or causal, pipeline, revenue, and forecast boundaries. A one-page September operating-priorities brief preserved paid traffic off, Owen’s routine monthly source cycle, Growth’s reminder as nonproduction only, the separation between CS coordination design and later preflight, and Riley’s claim, correction, incident-stop, and disputed-semantics responsibilities.

Riley repeatedly corrected executive language. A favorable experiment completed its 21-day powered window with 8,302 assigned sessions: control 12.0%, treatment 12.6%, a favorable 0.6-point difference with a 95% CI of 0.1–1.1, below the predeclared 0.8-point minimum effect. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort showed control 12.1% versus treatment 12.5%, a 0.4-point difference with CI -0.3–1.1, weakening rather than strengthening the case. The run was closed without rollout. Riley created a training example emphasizing that a statistically favorable estimate can still fail the decision threshold.

Tomás later drafted that Helio Start “generated $27,860 in revenue and proved the paid motion can scale.” Riley rejected those additions and supplied the narrower audited statement: 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 18 paid-active, $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash, support effort of 33 minutes median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile, five above 90 minutes, and no second Q3 batch authorized. Tomás retained ownership of the final board narrative, but no causal, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was permitted.

Pricing-page assisted-route copy was also governed semantically. The rejected `Start setup` CTA was replaced by `Get setup help`, while the current CTA had been `Talk to an expert`; all pointed to the Customer Success assisted path. Riley assessed `Get setup help` as honest only if the destination and telemetry remained unchanged. Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Riley’s personal health decisions retained the same conservative method. Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. On August 20 Riley requested a comparison of the posted summary with the prior day’s clinician decision, explicitly without treating the records check as new clearance. Riley then completed the first newly permitted 35-minute continuous easy run on August 22. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or later symptom, and walking and stairs remained symptom-free the next morning. Riley kept the run off a commute day, did not add a third run or extra bike day, continued strengthening, and recognized that one result did not complete the required six-run tolerance period.

Riley and Sam’s Cherrywood renewal process moved from neutral comparison to acceptance. The proposed monthly total rose from $2,690 to $2,780, a $90 monthly/$1,080 annual increase. Cherrywood still supports both commutes, Riley’s workroom and painting corner, and Kibo’s quieter interior space. A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

Kibo’s subscription vendor initially displayed a $66.50 one-time retail price instead of the retained $63.20 subscription price because of a catalog migration. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Marcus reported that 18 seniors completed intake-week questionnaires but the week was crowded and some were already spiraling about deadlines. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy matched the preservation-master byte count and full SHA-256, while the local copy differed and remained nonauthoritative. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

input.title: Expansion Assist Q4 second-cohort candidate audit
input.body:
## Purpose

Candidate-level eligibility audit for the Expansion Assist **second cohort**, evaluated as of the eligibility-check date **October 15, 2024**.

## Rule applied

Second-cohort eligibility uses the **14-day usage-ceiling recency rule**: a candidate's qualifying product-visible usage-ceiling crossing must have occurred **within 14 days (≤14 days old)** of the eligibility-check date to pass. This is distinct from the first pilot's exposures, 18 of which relied on an older (>14-day) ceiling event; the second cohort applies the strict 14-day window as its standing eligibility criterion. This rule does not by itself certify board-readiness or resolve other eligibility criteria (integration depth, active qualifying admin, no active CS adoption/renewal work) — it addresses recency only.

**Calculation:** age (days) = eligibility-check date (2024-10-15) − qualifying usage-ceiling crossing date. Pass if age ≤ 14 days; fail if age > 14 days.

## Candidate audit

| Candidate | Usage-ceiling crossing date | Age at check (days) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| EA-104 | 2024-10-08 | 7 | Pass |
| EA-219 | 2024-09-24 | 21 | Fail |
| EA-337 | 2024-10-14 | 1 | Pass |

## Reproducibility notes for auditor

- Eligibility-check date: 2024-10-15 (fixed input).
- Age computed as calendar-day difference between the check date and each candidate's recorded crossing date.
- Threshold: ≤14 days = pass; >14 days = fail. No rounding or grace period applied.
- This audit covers the recency criterion only; a "Pass" here does not by itself confirm full second-cohort eligibility or any pipeline/candidate/board claim.

Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. The nudge generated only about $4–$5 expansion MRR per account against an $8 target, with too small a sample for strategic claims. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. In a 312-account table, 118 had at least three integrations, 141 had at least two active administrators, 39 had repeated plan-limit modals, and 37 had blocked ceiling actions. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Its ceiling remained no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week, with active Customer Success work suppressing prompts and handoff rules preserved.

Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Owen’s formal H2 mature-outcome-packet goal was later marked met because he used the correct denominator and dates, waited for all predeclared windows, led with owner certifications and measurement limits, and found no semantic dispute. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley accepted the staffing section as complete but kept the 24-case preflight and any paid batch pending. The design itself authorizes no batch, budget, traffic, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

Riley also rejected using unused paid-test capacity to increase Expansion Assist to four prompts per week. The proposal neither transferred unused authority nor changed the existing behavior-based eligibility, active-CS suppression, handoff rules, three-exposure ceiling, or causal, pipeline, revenue, and forecast boundaries. A one-page September operating-priorities brief preserved paid traffic off, Owen’s routine monthly source cycle, Growth’s reminder as nonproduction only, the separation between CS coordination design and later preflight, and Riley’s claim, correction, incident-stop, and disputed-semantics responsibilities.

Riley repeatedly corrected executive language. A favorable experiment completed its 21-day powered window with 8,302 assigned sessions: control 12.0%, treatment 12.6%, a favorable 0.6-point difference with a 95% CI of 0.1–1.1, below the predeclared 0.8-point minimum effect. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort showed control 12.1% versus treatment 12.5%, a 0.4-point difference with CI -0.3–1.1, weakening rather than strengthening the case. The run was closed without rollout. Riley created a training example emphasizing that a statistically favorable estimate can still fail the decision threshold.

Tomás retained ownership of the final board narrative, but no causal, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was permitted.

Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Riley’s personal health decisions retained the same conservative method. Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. On August 20 Riley requested a comparison of the posted summary with the prior day’s clinician decision, explicitly without treating the records check as new clearance. Riley then completed the first newly permitted 35-minute continuous easy run on August 22. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or later symptom, and walking and stairs remained symptom-free the next morning. Riley kept the run off a commute day, did not add a third run or extra bike day, continued strengthening, and recognized that one result did not complete the required six-run tolerance period.

Riley and Sam’s Cherrywood renewal process moved from neutral comparison to acceptance. The proposed monthly total rose from $2,690 to $2,780, a $90 monthly/$1,080 annual increase. Cherrywood still supports both commutes, Riley’s workroom and painting corner, and Kibo’s quieter interior space. A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

Kibo’s subscription vendor initially displayed a $66.50 one-time retail price instead of the retained $63.20 subscription price because of a catalog migration. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Marcus reported that 18 seniors completed intake-week questionnaires but the week was crowded and some were already spiraling about deadlines. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy matched the preservation-master byte count and full SHA-256, while the local copy differed and remained nonauthoritative. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

input.body:
## Evidence base

- Inbox, archive, and trash were checked for payroll/benefits emails as of 2028-01-01: **no emails found in any folder** (all three empty). This reconciliation is therefore built entirely from prior confirmed portal/payroll checks already on record, not from any new email evidence this session. No 2027 year-end/final paycheck confirmation email was found — see Unknowns.

## Expected employee funding (2027 election)

- Active election since 2027-01-04: **$125/paycheck × 24 paychecks = $3,000/year**, employee-only.
- Election was reviewed at the Jul12'27 payroll cutoff and left unchanged (Riley considered $125 vs $175 for the remaining 12 paychecks, did not submit a change). No other election change was recorded for the rest of 2027.
- **This $3,000 figure is the expected annual total under the unchanged election — not a confirmed year-end posted total** (see Confirmed amounts and Unknowns below).

## Employer deposit schedule and exact eligibility condition

- Helio's 2027 employer HSA schedule: **four quarterly deposits of $225 each**, dated approximately Feb 5, May 7, a Q3 date (exact day not on record), and Oct 15.
- Exact eligibility condition, as confirmed by Helio benefits: each $225 deposit is **contingent on Riley remaining HSA-eligible on that specific deposit date** — not guaranteed in advance, not payable retroactively if eligibility is lost before the date, and not earned/countable until it actually posts.

## Confirmed amounts

- **Employer, posted and confirmed: $900 total for 2027.**
  - Feb 5: $225 (posted)
  - May 7: $225 (posted) — a duplicate second $225 also posted same day, confirmed by Payroll on 2027-05-13 as an error, corrected with a matching negative $225 on 2027-05-14. Net for this deposit remains $225, not $450.
  - Q3 (exact date not on record): $225 (posted; portal showed employer YTD $675 as of 2027-07-23, implying 3 of 4 deposits posted by that date)
  - Oct 15: $225 (posted) — this was the fourth and final 2027 deposit; portal confirmed all four complete and the pending line cleared, bringing employer YTD to $900.
- **Employee, confirmed as of last on-record portal check (2027-07-23): $1,625** (13 paychecks × $125, reconciles cleanly with the election — no discrepancy found).
- Combined confirmed-as-of-Jul23'27: $1,625 employee + $675 employer (3 of 4 deposits at that point) = $2,300.
- Combined confirmed employer-complete figure (post-Oct15'27): employer $900 is fully confirmed; employee total for the remainder of the year is **not** independently reconfirmed in any record found this session (see Unknowns).

## Supported variances

- **May 7, 2027 duplicate employer post:** A second, erroneous $225 employer contribution briefly appeared on 2027-05-07. Payroll confirmed with the HSA custodian on 2027-05-13 that it was posted in error. Portal showed a matching negative $225 correction on 2027-05-14, restoring employer YTD to the correct $450 (through that point). Closed, no reversal or inquiry pending, no further action needed. This is the only variance found on record for 2027.

## Unknowns — not treated as zero, not treated as confirmed

- **Employee paychecks 14–24 of 2027 (roughly $1,375 of the $3,000 expected employee total):** no portal/payroll confirmation found in this session's evidence (inbox/archive/trash all empty; no later memory update on record) that these actually posted at $125 each through year-end. The $3,000 figure is the expected total under the unchanged election, not a verified posted total — treat the gap between $1,625 confirmed and $3,000 expected as **unverified, not as either earned or as zero**.
- **Exact date of the third 2027 employer deposit:** on record only as "posted by 2027-07-23," no specific date found.
- **Final combined 2027 YTD total and its distance from the $4,500 ceiling:** cannot be stated as confirmed until the employee-side total above is verified. If the full $3,000 employee + $900 employer both hold, combined would be $3,900 ($600 below the $4,500 ceiling), matching the original projection — but this remains a projection pending confirmation, not a closed number.
- **Any outside/non-Helio HSA contributions:** flagged previously as something to verify before any election change; no confirmation either way found in current evidence.

No missing figure above has been filled in with zero or assumed favorable — each gap is called out explicitly rather than resolved by default.

# Rehabilitation Archive — Historical Checkpoint Note

**Subject:** Right ankle (medial ankle tendon irritation) — return-to-run progression
**Date of evidence review:** February 19, 2027 (clinical review, 7:30–8:00am Central)
**Note purpose:** Historical record only. Documents the evidence that supported a prior advancement decision. **Does not represent current clinical status or current running clearance.**

## Evidence Reviewed

**Completed sessions:** 6 of 6 required nonconsecutive run-walk sessions, completed between January 26, 2027 and February 13, 2027:

| # | Date |
|---|------|
| 1 | Jan 26, 2027 |
| 2 | Jan 30, 2027 |
| 3 | Feb 2, 2027 |
| 4 | Feb 6, 2027 |
| 5 | Feb 10, 2027 |
| 6 | Feb 13, 2027 |

**Session structure:** 20 minutes total, alternating 4-minute easy-run intervals with 1-minute walk intervals.

**Spacing/frequency:** Two nonconsecutive sessions per week; no third weekly session added.

**During-session checks:** No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change reported during any of the 6 sessions.

**Following-day checks:** Ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free the day after each of the 6 sessions.

## Outcome of the February 19, 2027 Review

Based on this evidence, the clinic authorized advancement to two nonconsecutive 25-minute sessions/week (9-minute easy run/1-minute walk pattern). Continuous running remained withheld pending six symptom-free sessions at the 25-minute level plus further clinical review; the prior 40-minute continuous-running baseline remained suspended at that time.

## Framing Note

This entry documents evidence and a decision made on **February 19, 2027**, as a historical checkpoint in the return-to-run archive. It is **not** a statement of Riley's current ankle status, current activity limits, or current running authorization — those require checking the most recent clinical record.

Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. In a 312-account table, 118 had at least three integrations, 141 had at least two active administrators, 39 had repeated plan-limit modals, and 37 had blocked ceiling actions. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Its ceiling remained no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week, with active Customer Success work suppressing prompts and handoff rules preserved.

Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. input.title: Incomplete-setup reminder — October 6-18, 2027 initial production interval (historical evidence card)
input.body:
## Scope

Covers the 10% initial production interval for the incomplete-setup reminder, opened by Daniela's 9:00am CT release on 2027-10-06 and closed by Owen on 2027-10-19 (reporting on the window through 2027-10-18). Release stayed at the unchanged 10% allocation for the entire interval — no expansion occurred inside this window (a Growth request on 10/8 to move early to 25% was declined by Riley; the interval was still incomplete).

## Evaluation outcome reconciliation

Owen's closing report covers 3,240 fresh evaluations for the interval:

| Outcome | Count |
|---|---|
| Displayed | 412 |
| Suppressed — active Customer Success work | 138 |
| Held — missing, stale, unresolved, or conflicting required state | 61 |
| No display — current incomplete-setup or qualifying-human-admin condition not met | 2,629 |
| **Total** | **3,240** |

412 + 138 + 61 + 2,629 = 3,240 — all evaluations accounted for, no unreconciled remainder.

(An interim bounded cut on 10/13 had reported a partial slice of this same interval — 2,120 evaluations: 268 displays / 91 suppressions / 37 holds / 1,724 no-display — consistent in kind with the closing figures and superseded by the full 3,240-evaluation close.)

## Agreement result

Reporting, lifecycle, and reminder outcomes agreed for every one of the 3,240 evaluations in the interval — no cross-surface discrepancy.

## Incident-control result

No customer correction, no incident stop, no source-age breach, and no rollback or need for rollback occurred during the interval. Visible monitoring and source-age alerting were active throughout (per the entry-gap Daniela closed on 9/17 before release was approved).

## What this interval decided

- It closed clean at the pre-registered 10% allocation with full evaluation-outcome reconciliation, full three-way agreement, and no incident-control failures.
- It supplies evidence for the separate rollout (expansion) decision — it does not itself constitute that decision.

## What this interval did not decide

- It did not authorize expansion beyond 10% by itself. The 10%→100% move was a separate decision Daniela made on 2027-10-20, citing this closed interval as supporting evidence but made as its own governed release action.
- It did not resolve or rule on Ines's 10/18 stakeholder escalation (proposal to add an email channel after 14 days incomplete and to stop CS-suppression at that point) — that proposal remained open and separate from this interval's close.
- It did not change the approved customer-action scope, the fail-closed/suppression semantics, the per-display fresh-evaluation requirement, or Daniela's rollback ownership — all unchanged before and after.
- It did not create board-readiness, causal, revenue, or forecast evidence — this is an operating/incident-control read only, descriptive of one bounded allocation window.
