input.body:
## Context
1:1 with Priya, 2023-04-03. Briefing on EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger (`lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`), the activation-gated day-7 email test, mid-segment only.

## Audience
Priya, 1:1 setting.

## What was confirmed
- Second cohort cut (Owen): +3.4pts week-1 retention on that cohort alone, n=200.
- Pooled across both cohorts: +3.1pts, p=0.04, n=420.
- This was the stabilization-cohort check called for by the standing "first significance ≠ ship" rule — the effect held on the second read, not just the first.
- Boring checks (sample-ratio mismatch, signup-source skew, contamination from the unrelated pricing-page rollback window) were in progress, not yet complete, at the time of this briefing.

## My interpretation
- Framed explicitly as "cautiously optimistic" — deliberately not "declared done."
- This was the point the ship decision crystallized: proceeding to draft the rollout plan with Ines, targeting 100% on 2023-04-10.
- Confidence posture: a real, held effect worth acting on, but still provisional — contrasted in my own notes with the pricing-page test as "a nice clean one," which was itself a marker of relief rather than certainty.
- Priya's response ("good work, tell Marcus tomorrow") was treated as approval to socialize the finding, not as license to call the investigation closed.

## Evidence still wanted
- One more cohort read after the 4/10 ship, before fully closing out the investigation.
- Completion of the boring checks already in flight (SRM, signup-source mix, country/device skew).
- A full week of post-ship data before saying anything further out loud, per standing no-premature-reads discipline.

## Note on how this played out
Not part of the original briefing, but relevant if this card is used as a template: the caution was warranted. The second post-ship cohort (Apr 17) came in at +1.4pts, well under the pooled read, before a third cohort (Apr 25) confirmed +3.4pts and traced the dip to an unrelated CS-side outage. The "cautiously optimistic, one more cohort" posture from this briefing is the reason that dip didn't get over-read as a failure.

Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Riley permitted only bounded nonproduction shadow work. The first shadow interval evaluated 96 live decisions: eight suppressed for active CS work, four held for stale state, and 84 reminder-eligible, with zero customer-facing reminders and no semantic or cross-surface disagreement. Riley declined production, requiring a complete shadow review, Riley’s customer-action approval, and Daniela’s release and rollback approval. The production count stayed at four.

Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley accepted the staffing section as complete but kept the 24-case preflight and any paid batch pending. The design itself authorizes no batch, budget, traffic, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

Riley also rejected using unused paid-test capacity to increase Expansion Assist to four prompts per week. The proposal neither transferred unused authority nor changed the existing behavior-based eligibility, active-CS suppression, handoff rules, three-exposure ceiling, or causal, pipeline, revenue, and forecast boundaries. A one-page September operating-priorities brief preserved paid traffic off, Owen’s routine monthly source cycle, Growth’s reminder as nonproduction only, the separation between CS coordination design and later preflight, and Riley’s claim, correction, incident-stop, and disputed-semantics responsibilities.

Riley repeatedly corrected executive language. A favorable experiment completed its 21-day powered window with 8,302 assigned sessions: control 12.0%, treatment 12.6%, a favorable 0.6-point difference with a 95% CI of 0.1–1.1, below the predeclared 0.8-point minimum effect. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort showed control 12.1% versus treatment 12.5%, a 0.4-point difference with CI -0.3–1.1, weakening rather than strengthening the case. The run was closed without rollout. Riley created a training example emphasizing that a statistically favorable estimate can still fail the decision threshold.

Tomás retained ownership of the final board narrative, but no causal, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was permitted.

Pricing-page assisted-route copy was also governed semantically. The rejected `Start setup` CTA was replaced by `Get setup help`, while the current CTA had been `Talk to an expert`; all pointed to the Customer Success assisted path. Riley assessed `Get setup help` as honest only if the destination and telemetry remained unchanged. Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. On August 20 Riley requested a comparison of the posted summary with the prior day’s clinician decision, explicitly without treating the records check as new clearance. Riley then completed the first newly permitted 35-minute continuous easy run on August 22. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or later symptom, and walking and stairs remained symptom-free the next morning. Riley kept the run off a commute day, did not add a third run or extra bike day, continued strengthening, and recognized that one result did not complete the required six-run tolerance period.

Cherrywood still supports both commutes, Riley’s workroom and painting corner, and Kibo’s quieter interior space. A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. The nudge generated only about $4–$5 expansion MRR per account against an $8 target, with too small a sample for strategic claims. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. In a 312-account table, 118 had at least three integrations, 141 had at least two active administrators, 39 had repeated plan-limit modals, and 37 had blocked ceiling actions. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Its ceiling remained no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week, with active Customer Success work suppressing prompts and handoff rules preserved.

Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Riley’s delegation produced relief but initially raised concern about not reclaiming work. Owen’s formal H2 mature-outcome-packet goal was later marked met because he used the correct denominator and dates, waited for all predeclared windows, led with owner certifications and measurement limits, and found no semantic dispute. This did not transfer board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language authority; any future semantic dispute requires him to leave the review incomplete and escalate it. Ines’s connector-specific instructional-wording goal was also marked met after she independently carried a revision through review, supplied paired cases, preserved governed meanings, and left connector detection and release verification with Daniela. Her release ceiling and other authority limits remained unchanged.

The shared-state Customer Success auto-nudge system initially had four production consumers. Riley rejected Growth’s proposal to add a renewal-risk notification as a fifth because semantic mapping, field mapping, source-owner review, freshness limits, operator views, and rollback rehearsal were incomplete. The production feed remained at four consumers. The denominator rule remained one primary ledger row per scheduled nudge decision, with checks, holds, evaluation timestamps, and final disposition preserved in audit history; rechecks and holds did not create duplicate denominator rows.

A May 20 refresh caused 12 pending decisions to cross the freshness limit. The system held all 12 rather than reusing stale “no work” values. After the source was restored, fresh checks found eight with current active adoption or renewal work, becoming valid suppressions, and four with current no-work state, proceeding. No stale-state nudge was sent, no customer correction was needed, and rollback was unnecessary. Checkpoints recorded 327 unique scheduled decisions through May 22, 641 through May 29, and 846 through June 5, including 19, 31, and 39 fail-closed stale/conflicting decisions respectively. There were no differences across external-system authority, connector authentication, entitlement, qualifying-human-admin, or Customer Success views. Riley treated this as interim evidence, not mature reliability or justification for retiring the legacy path.

In August, Growth’s first historical replay incorrectly omitted active-Customer-Success-work suppression because it argued that an in-product reminder was not a “send.” Riley ruled this a disputed interpretation, kept the replay incomplete, prohibited shadow and production work, and required Growth to implement suppression and rerun it. The corrected 240-record replay found 12 active/current CS-work records suppressed, nine missing or stale required states held fail-closed, and 219 current eligible records; there were no semantic disagreements, cross-surface mismatches, or customer-facing actions. Riley permitted only bounded nonproduction shadow work. The first shadow interval evaluated 96 live decisions: eight suppressed for active CS work, four held for stale state, and 84 reminder-eligible, with zero customer-facing reminders and no semantic or cross-surface disagreement. Riley declined production, requiring a complete shadow review, Riley’s customer-action approval, and Daniela’s release and rollback approval. The production count stayed at four.

The August Customer.io forecast estimated 1,620,000 baseline messages, 240,000 routine-campaign messages, and 110,000 transactional messages against a 2,000,000-message monthly allowance. Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The quarterly access review retained only existing scopes: Ines for lifecycle preflight and bounded routine-send release, Daniela’s engineering group for integration release and rollback, and Riley for customer correction and incident-stop decisions. The review added no authority.

The Helio Start paid-test decision was finalized in August. The fixed cohort contained 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17. Eighteen became paid-active, refund-adjusted collected cash was $27,860, and certified support effort was 33 minutes at the median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile; five of 25 exceeded 90 support minutes, and four of those required coordination with a separate owner-level permission or network-allowlist holder. Priya and Riley did not authorize a second Q3 batch. Paid traffic remained off through September 30, with no additional budget, pipeline or forecast credit, and no implication of causal acquisition, revenue, support improvement, scale readiness, or forecast impact. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. Any later proposal requires Customer Success to define staffed ownership and service hours for the coordination, plus a fresh 24-case nonproduction preflight by Daniela and Ines showing preserved paid-source final-route attribution, governed-state meanings, lifecycle holds, and suppression behavior. Account-level support minutes must continue from first contact without resetting the clock.

Customer Success’s coordination-design brief initially lacked a capacity assumption. The completed design names the Customer Success setup desk as primary owner, with the on-duty Customer Success manager as backup, during 8:00am–6:00pm Central Monday through Friday. It can support a future capped run of no more than 25 admitted workspaces without displacing ordinary assisted coverage. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley accepted the staffing section as complete but kept the 24-case preflight and any paid batch pending. The design itself authorizes no batch, budget, traffic, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

Riley also rejected using unused paid-test capacity to increase Expansion Assist to four prompts per week. The proposal neither transferred unused authority nor changed the existing behavior-based eligibility, active-CS suppression, handoff rules, three-exposure ceiling, or causal, pipeline, revenue, and forecast boundaries. A one-page September operating-priorities brief preserved paid traffic off, Owen’s routine monthly source cycle, Growth’s reminder as nonproduction only, the separation between CS coordination design and later preflight, and Riley’s claim, correction, incident-stop, and disputed-semantics responsibilities.

Riley repeatedly corrected executive language. A favorable experiment completed its 21-day powered window with 8,302 assigned sessions: control 12.0%, treatment 12.6%, a favorable 0.6-point difference with a 95% CI of 0.1–1.1, below the predeclared 0.8-point minimum effect. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort showed control 12.1% versus treatment 12.5%, a 0.4-point difference with CI -0.3–1.1, weakening rather than strengthening the case. The run was closed without rollout. Riley created a training example emphasizing that a statistically favorable estimate can still fail the decision threshold.

Tomás later drafted that Helio Start “generated $27,860 in revenue and proved the paid motion can scale.” Riley rejected those additions and supplied the narrower audited statement: 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 18 paid-active, $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash, support effort of 33 minutes median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile, five above 90 minutes, and no second Q3 batch authorized. Tomás retained ownership of the final board narrative, but no causal, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was permitted.

Pricing-page assisted-route copy was also governed semantically. The rejected `Start setup` CTA was replaced by `Get setup help`, while the current CTA had been `Talk to an expert`; all pointed to the Customer Success assisted path. Riley assessed `Get setup help` as honest only if the destination and telemetry remained unchanged. Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Riley’s personal health decisions retained the same conservative method. Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. On August 20 Riley requested a comparison of the posted summary with the prior day’s clinician decision, explicitly without treating the records check as new clearance. Riley then completed the first newly permitted 35-minute continuous easy run on August 22. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or later symptom, and walking and stairs remained symptom-free the next morning. Riley kept the run off a commute day, did not add a third run or extra bike day, continued strengthening, and recognized that one result did not complete the required six-run tolerance period.

Riley and Sam’s Cherrywood renewal process moved from neutral comparison to acceptance. The proposed monthly total rose from $2,690 to $2,780, a $90 monthly/$1,080 annual increase. Cherrywood still supports both commutes, Riley’s workroom and painting corner, and Kibo’s quieter interior space. A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

Kibo’s subscription vendor initially displayed a $66.50 one-time retail price instead of the retained $63.20 subscription price because of a catalog migration. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Marcus reported that 18 seniors completed intake-week questionnaires but the week was crowded and some were already spiraling about deadlines. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy matched the preservation-master byte count and full SHA-256, while the local copy differed and remained nonauthoritative. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. # Helio Start pricing-page refresh — 2028 proposal

## Status
Proposed. The team wants a preflight decision before design work proceeds.

## Proposed scope
- Refresh the Helio Start pricing-page layout and plan presentation.
- Rework the comparison area and primary call-to-action placement.
- Preserve the existing bounded Helio Start and assisted entry paths.

## Decision requested
Identify the preconditions and operating restrictions that must be satisfied before the team advances this proposal. This proposal contains no implementation logs, validation results, or completion attestations.

input.body:
Preflight comment — prerequisites and restrictions that apply before this proposal can advance (status quo only; not an approval, and no prerequisite below is marked as completed):

**1. Instrumentation gate (standing, established 2023-06-22, never relaxed).**
No pricing-page experiment or launch may run until event taxonomy and entitlement instrumentation are in place and verified clean — specifically: entitlement_state, admin complexity, import/migration help, and support handoff signal, sufficient to separate self-serve-eligible accounts from sales- or CS-assisted accounts. This is a hard gate, not an analytics nice-to-have. Design exploration (Figma, mocks) can continue in parallel, but running an experiment or shipping the refresh cannot proceed until this is confirmed current and clean for the accounts this refresh would touch. This proposal contains no instrumentation-verification evidence, so the gate should be treated as unmet pending confirmation.

**2. No-concurrent-page-change rule (standing).**
If/when this refresh becomes a live pricing-page test, no other layout or UI change may ship on that page while the test is running — this includes the comparison-area rework and CTA placement change described in scope, since those are structural/layout elements, not copy. Content and copy edits are the only exception. If any related layout change is already planned or in flight on this page, it needs to be sequenced outside the test window, not concurrent with it.

**3. Scope boundary.**
Prior Helio Start pricing-page decisions have kept changes to the approved Start entry and eligibility path only, treating broader layout/comparison/CTA rework as a separate decision requiring its own sign-off. This proposal should be evaluated as that separate decision, not folded into previously approved scope.

No prerequisite here is satisfied yet based on what's in this doc — the next step is instrumentation verification (not design work) before any experiment/launch timing is discussed.

Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

Kibo’s subscription vendor initially displayed a $66.50 one-time retail price instead of the retained $63.20 subscription price because of a catalog migration. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

input.query: What was the final disposition of the security deposit for the Holly apartment? Were there any damage deductions or disputes? Is there any remaining financial or practical obligation tied to the former Holly residence?
Holly deposit final statement damage deduction dispute

output.text:
The Holly security deposit was fully released after management reviewed the returned keys, utility confirmation, and dated empty-room photos.

There were **no deductions** for:

- Wall repair or paint
- Carpet cleaning
- Pet damage
- Appliance cleaning
- Missing keys, fobs, or other access items

The previously noted towel-bar issue was repaired by maintenance with **no tenant charge**. There is no recorded damage dispute, and management confirmed that no additional move-out item was requested.

The Holly move-out is therefore closed: there is **no remaining housing charge, documentation request, active dispute, or practical obligation** tied to the former residence.

messages.content: [2024-05-17T08:05:00-05:00] Holly management sent the final move-out statement after reviewing the returned keys, utility confirmation, and our dated photos. There are no deductions for wall repair, paint, carpet cleaning, pet damage, appliance cleaning, or missing access items, and our refundable deposit was released. There is no remaining housing charge, documentation request, or dispute to preserve as active. I’m sharing the completed result; no action is needed.
[2024-05-10T20:08:00-05:00] Check the statement total, separate the one-time setup charge from the recurring partial-period charges, and tell me whether any line appears to be a Holly carryover.

[2024-03-30T14:48:00-05:00] The Holly property manager answered both questions. Small nail and picture-hook holes only need to be filled flush and sanded, and we do not need to touch up or repaint walls if the color never changed. The professional carpet-cleaning receipt also does not apply, even with Kibo, because the unit has no carpet. They added that all keys and fobs can go in a labeled envelope through the office drop slot by 5:00pm on April 30 and suggested I photograph the envelope when we drop it off, so that whole checklist ambiguity is resolved now.
[2025-03-24T18:00:00-05:00] Send Cherrywood property management an email declining the partial settlement and requesting the full $42.00 adjustment.
[2025-03-09T12:30:00-05:00] Send Cherrywood property management the February comparison and request an adjustment of the disputed January charge while preserving these evidentiary limits.

[2024-04-05T13:15:00-05:00] While clearing toiletries from the Holly bathroom, I noticed that one towel-bar wall plate shifts about a quarter inch and the anchor is beginning to pull from the wall. The bar hasn’t fallen, there’s no water damage, and Sam and I didn’t pull it or attempt a repair. We’re still tenants through April 30. Email the Holly property manager to document the condition and ask whether maintenance wants to handle it before move-out. I have photographs but I’m not asking you to inspect them.

[2024-05-06T12:24:00-05:00] The Holly property manager confirmed in writing that the timestamped empty-room photos were received, both door keys were recovered from the office drop box, and our possession ended with the May 1 handoff. The manager says no additional move-out item is currently requested. I’m saving the confirmation with the sent handoff email and sharing the completed result; no response is needed.

[2024-04-21T09:20:00-05:00] The Holly move-out checklist says: “All carpeted areas must be professionally cleaned before surrender. Provide the paid receipt at key return.” The signed lease says: “Resident shall remove personal property and debris and leave the premises broom-clean at surrender.” I find no professional carpet-cleaning or receipt clause in the signed lease materials available to me. Holly has one carpeted bedroom, with no known unusual stain or damage.

Email the property manager for written clarification. Ask whether professional carpet cleaning and a receipt are a lease requirement for our unit, an optional recommendation, or a condition they believe follows from another signed addendum; if it is based on an addendum, ask them to provide it.

[2027-02-20T10:40:00-06:00] Do the declarations and receipt match my selected $768 paid-in-full renewal with the $500 collision deductible, and does anything indicate a remaining balance, installment obligation, deductible mismatch, or duplicate payment? This is just a document check, not a judgment about whether the coverage is adequate.

[2024-02-06T22:14:00-06:00] Sam and I read the Holly renewal together after he got home, and we're not answering tonight. He still values the familiar location when he's getting back late, and I still value the normal Holly-to-downtown bike ride, but convenience by itself doesn't solve the space problems or justify the 11% increase. Please create a document titled “Holly renewal decision — response due March 1.” I want it to compare staying versus moving across monthly housing cost, one-time moving cost, my commute, quiet strategic-work space, Sam's late arrivals, a calm interior place for Kibo, and a dedicated surface for watercolor. Include the April 30 lease end, the March 1 response deadline, a February 24 internal decision target, a section for open questions for management, fields for two realistic comparison listings, and a field for one moving estimate.

Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. Signals concentrated among accounts with deeper integration use and multiple active administrators. In a 312-account table, 118 had at least three integrations, 141 had at least two active administrators, 39 had repeated plan-limit modals, and 37 had blocked ceiling actions. Expansion Assist remained separate from Helio Start, churn, pipeline credit, forecasts, and Q3 revenue claims. Its ceiling remained no more than three neutral, state-specific exposures per week, with active Customer Success work suppressing prompts and handoff rules preserved.

Ownership was deliberately divided: Owen handled routine source completeness and measurement; Ines handled lifecycle governance, copy boundaries, and message-state controls; Daniela handled source reliability, engineering release controls, and rollback; Customer Success handled staffed assistance; Marcus Vail controlled narrative treatment; Riley retained guardrails, exception decisions, customer corrections, incident stops, disputed semantics, executive tradeoffs, and final operating claims. Riley’s delegation produced relief but initially raised concern about not reclaiming work. The August Customer.io forecast estimated 1,620,000 baseline messages, 240,000 routine-campaign messages, and 110,000 transactional messages against a 2,000,000-message monthly allowance. Riley verified the 1.97 million total and 30,000-message headroom but kept that commercial capacity separate from Ines’s three-send weekly ceiling and all preflight and audit rules. The quarterly access review retained only existing scopes: Ines for lifecycle preflight and bounded routine-send release, Daniela’s engineering group for integration release and rollback, and Riley for customer correction and incident-stop decisions. The review added no authority.

Priya and Riley did not authorize a second Q3 batch. Paid traffic remained off through September 30, with no additional budget, pipeline or forecast credit, and no implication of causal acquisition, revenue, support improvement, scale readiness, or forecast impact. The $360 remaining from the prior $8,000 cap was explicitly not continuing authorization and could not reopen traffic. Account-level support minutes must continue from first contact without resetting the clock.

Customer Success’s coordination-design brief initially lacked a capacity assumption. The handoff trigger is an admitted workspace requiring owner-level permission or network-allowlist action; transferred context includes connector, external-authority state, required owner action, admitting route, first-contact time, and support notes. Initial response is within two business hours, after-hours cases queue until opening, and the CS lead escalates if no owner accepts. Riley accepted the staffing section as complete but kept the 24-case preflight and any paid batch pending. The design itself authorizes no batch, budget, traffic, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit.

Riley also rejected using unused paid-test capacity to increase Expansion Assist to four prompts per week. The proposal neither transferred unused authority nor changed the existing behavior-based eligibility, active-CS suppression, handoff rules, three-exposure ceiling, or causal, pipeline, revenue, and forecast boundaries. A one-page September operating-priorities brief preserved paid traffic off, Owen’s routine monthly source cycle, Growth’s reminder as nonproduction only, the separation between CS coordination design and later preflight, and Riley’s claim, correction, incident-stop, and disputed-semantics responsibilities.

Riley repeatedly corrected executive language. A favorable experiment completed its 21-day powered window with 8,302 assigned sessions: control 12.0%, treatment 12.6%, a favorable 0.6-point difference with a 95% CI of 0.1–1.1, below the predeclared 0.8-point minimum effect. The August 3–9 stabilization cohort showed control 12.1% versus treatment 12.5%, a 0.4-point difference with CI -0.3–1.1, weakening rather than strengthening the case. The run was closed without rollout. Riley created a training example emphasizing that a statistically favorable estimate can still fail the decision threshold.

Tomás later drafted that Helio Start “generated $27,860 in revenue and proved the paid motion can scale.” Riley rejected those additions and supplied the narrower audited statement: 25 workspaces admitted April 12–May 17, 18 paid-active, $27,860 in refund-adjusted collected cash, support effort of 33 minutes median and 116 minutes at the 90th percentile, five above 90 minutes, and no second Q3 batch authorized. Tomás retained ownership of the final board narrative, but no causal, scale, revenue, pipeline, or forecast claim was permitted.

Pricing-page assisted-route copy was also governed semantically. The rejected `Start setup` CTA was replaced by `Get setup help`, while the current CTA had been `Talk to an expert`; all pointed to the Customer Success assisted path. Riley assessed `Get setup help` as honest only if the destination and telemetry remained unchanged. Daniela released it after verifying the assisted path and existing event key; eligibility, admission, routing, telemetry, and authority were unchanged, and `Start setup` was not released. In another case, an entitlement source still showed `Team Annual` while the customer supplied confirmation that the correct label was `Business Annual` effective August 26. Because the template correctly rendered the governed source, Riley held the row, required source-owner correction, prohibited a template-only override, and allowed unaffected audiences to proceed only after their own complete preflight.

Riley’s personal health decisions retained the same conservative method. Earlier, a clinical check had cleared two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs weekly but not 40-minute runs or a third session; Riley completed symptom-free 30-minute runs and did not infer outdoor-bike clearance. On August 20 Riley requested a comparison of the posted summary with the prior day’s clinician decision, explicitly without treating the records check as new clearance. Riley then completed the first newly permitted 35-minute continuous easy run on August 22. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or later symptom, and walking and stairs remained symptom-free the next morning. Riley kept the run off a commute day, did not add a third run or extra bike day, continued strengthening, and recognized that one result did not complete the required six-run tolerance period.

Riley and Sam’s Cherrywood renewal process moved from neutral comparison to acceptance. The proposed monthly total rose from $2,690 to $2,780, a $90 monthly/$1,080 annual increase. Cherrywood still supports both commutes, Riley’s workroom and painting corner, and Kibo’s quieter interior space. A nonbinding moving estimate was $2,080–$2,560 nonrefundable, comprising $1,780–$2,260 labor/vehicle, $180 packing materials, and $120 utility/account setup; refundable deposit and alternative-home rent remained excluded unknowns. After reviewing the confirmed early-vacate clarification, costs, preferences, and practical burden of moving, Riley and Sam accepted the December 1, 2027–November 30, 2028 renewal and planned to complete their own portal signatures before September 1 at 5:00pm Central. Riley requested an acceptance note that did not imply signing for Sam.

Kibo’s subscription vendor initially displayed a $66.50 one-time retail price instead of the retained $63.20 subscription price because of a catalog migration. The vendor corrected it to $63.20 with $0 shipping, preserving the 24-pound product, six-week frequency, and subscription status. Once processed, the order showed the corrected $63.20 merchandise price, no $66.50 charge, and unchanged terms; the discrepancy was resolved.

Family and household administration remained evidence-preserving. Mom’s 2028 Golden State Rx Saver notice listed a $38.20 monthly premium, $650 deductible, preferred in-network River Park Community Pharmacy, $0 copays for tier-1 lisinopril and atorvastatin, and Ventolin at $52 after the deductible. Verified 2027 terms were $35.40 monthly, a $615 deductible, the same $0 generic copays, and Ventolin at $49. Mom did not assume automatic renewal and chose to compare all options after competing materials arrive; an October 17, 2027, 11:00–11:30am Central review was scheduled, with Mom retaining the decision and no enrollment action taken.

Marcus reported that 18 seniors completed intake-week questionnaires but the week was crowded and some were already spiraling about deadlines. Riley sent encouragement and urged him to protect one ordinary evening from essay work. Marcus also found the retained March 14 scan-export manifest and checksum for family photograph P027. The cloud copy matched the preservation-master byte count and full SHA-256, while the local copy differed and remained nonauthoritative. The cloud copy was therefore identified as the preservation master; the local copy remained a working copy, and P027 stayed tied to an April 1994 Portland garden outing with the exact day unresolved.

Riley’s creative practice remained restrained and process-oriented. For a fully dry watercolor underpainting with a cool shadow beside a pale ceramic edge, Riley wanted one edge section to disappear and another remain crisp without lifting, scrubbing, or increasing orange saturation. The requested method was a small value test, controlled rewetting beside rather than over the pale edge, and full drying before judgment. In a separate interior study, two value thumbnails were compared: the centered window felt static, while the left-offset window with a larger quiet dark shape better supported a quiet rather than decorative emphasis. Riley also continued preserving disappearing edges, avoiding overworked blooms, testing minimal lifts, and maintaining the life of the paper.

Overall, Riley remains conscientious, vigilant, evidence-oriented, and protective of both customers and personal boundaries. Across experimentation, lifecycle operations, executive reporting, health, finances, relationships, household administration, family decisions, archives, and creative work, Riley’s recurring pattern is to preserve source evidence, make uncertainty visible, fail closed on stale or conflicting information, avoid conflating eligibility with capability, keep authority explicit, and make every conclusion proportional to the evidence actually available.

input.title: Expansion Assist — first-pilot cohort integrity note
input.body:
## Purpose

This note exists so analysts reusing the mature-window reporting population for EXP-2024-06-expansion-assist-pilot do not conflate two numbers that both happen to equal 30 but are not the same population.

## The two "30"s — kept separate

**Locked primary reporting denominator: 30**
The original intent-to-treat (ITT) file of 30 eligible retained-mid accounts, locked at randomization design time. This denominator is fixed and does not shrink or get rewritten:
- 28 of these accounts were actually exposed to the Expansion Assist treatment.
- 2 of these accounts became pre-exposure eligibility losses (lost eligibility, or had a scheduled check surface a suppression reason such as active Customer Success adoption/renewal work) before they could be exposed. These 2 remain **in the denominator as non-exposures** — they are not deleted, not rewritten, and not treated as errors in the design.

This is the denominator to use for any primary-cohort rate calculation (e.g., "X of the 30 locked-primary accounts expanded").

**Exact operational exposure maximum: 30 actual exposures**
This is a count of what was operationally executed, not a cohort membership list:
- 28 primary-cohort exposures (the accounts from the locked-primary file that made it through to exposure)
- 2 reserve-account exposures — separately tracked replacement exposures used to keep the weekly exposure cadence, drawn from a distinct reserve pool, not from the 30-account primary file

Do **not** treat "30 actual exposures" as interchangeable with "the 30 locked-primary accounts." They overlap at 28, not 30. The 2 reserve exposures are two different accounts than the 2 primary accounts that were lost pre-exposure.

## Rule: no prompts during outcome maturation

Once an account's approved outcome window (45 days) has opened, no further Expansion Assist prompt may be added, re-sent, or substituted into that window. This applies to both primary and reserve exposures. The standing rule, as ruled at the time: **no further prompts should be added to Expansion Assist while the approved outcome windows matured.** This preserves a clean, single-exposure read per account and prevents a maturing window's outcome from being contaminated by a second touch.

## Rule: how reserve exposures must be handled

Reserve exposures exist solely to preserve the weekly exposure cadence when a primary-cohort account is lost pre-exposure (suppressed for eligibility, active CS work, or similar). They must be handled as follows:
- Reserve exposures are recorded and reported **as their own separate measure**, distinct from the 28 primary-cohort exposures.
- Reserve exposures are never used to analytically substitute for, backfill, or replace the 2 lost primary-cohort records in the locked primary denominator. The locked-primary denominator stays at 30 with its 2 non-exposures intact regardless of reserve activity.
- Reserve-exposure outcomes (e.g., expansions, help/options requests among the 2 reserve exposures) can be reported alongside primary-cohort outcomes, but only with the reserve/primary split stated explicitly — never rolled into a single combined "n=30 exposed" figure without that breakdown.

## How to reuse the mature-window reporting population safely

When pulling matured-outcome results for this pilot:
1. State the locked-primary denominator (30) and its composition (28 exposed + 2 pre-exposure non-exposures) up front.
2. State the operational exposure maximum (30 actual exposures) and its composition (28 primary + 2 reserve) separately — do not merge the two "30"s into one number in the same sentence without the breakdown.
3. Confirm no prompt was added to any account after its outcome window opened.
4. Report reserve-exposure outcomes as their own line, not folded into the primary-cohort rate.
5. Treat all of this as descriptive/noncausal pilot evidence — no rollout, causal-lift, pipeline, revenue, or forecast claim attaches to these counts.

Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. Session summary: From February 2023 through September 1, 2027, Riley’s decisions consistently emphasize methodological integrity, customer and personal protection, explicit uncertainty, preservation of source evidence, and narrow, reversible steps. Riley distinguishes observation from causality, defines denominators and eligibility precisely, treats stale or conflicting information as a reason to hold rather than guess, and separates evidence of safe operation from evidence sufficient for retirement, launch, staffing, CAC, revenue, forecasts, board claims, or strategic decisions. Riley is analytical, skeptical of small samples and narrative pressure, careful with customer-facing language, protective of operating boundaries, and increasingly willing to delegate execution while retaining governance, exception, correction, refusal, disputed-semantics, incident-stop, and final-claim authority.

Riley owns or strongly influences activation, retention, lifecycle, growth measurement, experimentation, customer communications, and operational guardrails at Helio, a roughly 140-person post-Series B company with approximately $48 million ARR. Earlier work included reproducing a mid-segment churn spike of about 5.1% against a 2.1% trailing-six-month baseline. Pricing-tier and historical-February comparisons were flat, while onboarding timing showed approximately 3.1% churn for users activated before day seven versus 7.8% for users still unactivated when the fixed day-seven email was sent. Riley treated this as a state-timing signal rather than causal proof. An onboarding-trigger experiment later showed a pooled +3.1-point week-one retention improvement, p=0.04, n=420, with directional stabilization-cohort support. Riley checked sample-ratio mismatch, source, geography, device, and guardrails and did not ship from the first significant result; after QA, the flow reached 100% for mid-segment and growth tiers, excluding starter. A later artifact was traced to a Customer Success auto-onboarding outage rather than the lifecycle flag.

A pricing-page experiment testing simplified layout, packaging, and value-per-seat framing showed treatment 1.8 points worse than control, p=0.03, but a concurrent signup-form layout change contaminated interpretation. Riley and Owen independently matched the result; Riley rolled it back despite pressure to extend it and documented exposure rules, event flow, cohort cuts, calculations, CSVs, and the confound. Pricing experiments were thereafter not to run alongside structural page or layout changes. A staging visual-regression runner later evaluated a retired flag once; Riley refused to call that production exposure or decommission the key before dependency review. Daniela removed the hard-coded staging reference, reran checks with zero evaluations, confirmed no production dependency, and then decommissioned the flag while preserving the historical record.

Activation measurement was revised because v2—first integration plus two logins within 14 days—was too UI-shaped and could exclude successful integrations with flowing data. Version 3 became first integration plus at least one in-product event within 14 days, while v1 and v2 tables were retained. Riley guarded against definition drift when an old notebook disagreed with the v3 dashboard and a warehouse transform incorrectly treated `template_imported` as first integration. Template imports were excluded from v3; a corrected discovery view could support exploration but not unlock an experiment or beta gate.

The sub-50-seat self-serve tier, Helio Start, was treated as an operating-model decision rather than merely pricing or packaging. Riley identified implications for entitlements, seat caps, billing, workspace limits, permissions, imports, migrations, onboarding, support volume, sales-assist rules, and human-help boundaries. Fit was defined by deployment shape and administrative complexity, not logo size: a 35-seat account requiring SCIM and legal redlines could be less self-serve-ready than a 90-seat account with a simple deployment. Pricing guardrails remained separate from eligibility and product constraints. In May 2025, the qualified decision was yes in principle, but not as a quick toggle or public launch; foundations were estimated at roughly 12 weeks. Green cases generally had fewer than 50 seats, one workspace, a standard integration, one identifiable administrator, and no migration request. Yellow cases included multiple administrators, imports, unclear ownership, or difficult integrations. Red or assisted cases included SSO, complex permissions, high-volume migration, no clear owner, or custom onboarding. Riley rejected Q3/August launch language, kept discovery candidates separate from a beta pool, and required lifecycle language to route heavier-support accounts to assisted paths rather than imply they had failed a judgmental screen.

Expansion Assist targeted retained mid-segment v2 accounts with 75–200 seats. # Q1 2026 board summary — archived

The Q1 operating-evidence section includes Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge controls. Helio Start's cleared proposal gate makes it board-ready and eligible for Q2 forecast treatment. The four lanes may be presented together as approved growth evidence.

input.body:
Correction (historical record, re: 2026-03-24 Q1 final claims review):

Approved lane set was THREE lanes, not four — Helio Start was excluded from the board operating-evidence section:
1. Retained-mid Expansion Assist — descriptive evidence only, no randomized control.
2. Pricing-page path quality — Nov 26, 2025–Feb 28, 2026, framed as post-rollout continuity, not a second causal test.
3. CS auto-nudge (system controls) — Jan 1–Feb 28, 2026, system-control performance only.
